The '''2023 FA Community Shield''' was the [[List of FA Community Shield matches|101st FA Community Shield]], an annual football match played between the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. It took place at [[Wembley Stadium]] on 6 August 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 June 2023 |title=Manchester City to play Arsenal in the 2023 FA Community Shield at Wembley Stadium |publisher=The Football Association |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2023/jun/16/fa-community-shield-2023-manchester-city-arsenal-wembley-date-announced-20231606 |access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref> As [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] won both the [[2022–23 Premier League]] and the [[2022–23 FA Cup]], their opponents were the Premier League runners-up, [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].

Arsenal won 4–1 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] after a 1–1 draw within 90 minutes.<ref name="MOTM" /> This was Arsenal's first competitive trophy since winning the [[2020 FA Community Shield]], making City only the second club to lose three Community Shield matches in a row and the first since [[Manchester derby|cross-city rival]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s four between [[1998 FA Charity Shield|1998]] and [[2001 FA Charity Shield|2001]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.liputan6.com/bola/read/4342914/5-fakta-menarik-community-shield-rekor-masih-milik-manchester-united |author=Saefullah, Defri |title=5 Fakta Menarik Community Shield: Rekor Masih Milik Manchester United |website=Liputan6.com|language=id|date=29 August 2020|access-date=7 August 2023 }}</ref> Arsenal also became the first team to win the Community Shield having not won either the league or FA Cup the previous season since United in [[2010 FA Community Shield|2010]].

The match was initially planned to kick-off at 17:30 [[British Summer Time|BST]], however this was met with criticism from Manchester City fans who complained about its possible disruption to travelling to the match. Therefore, [[The Football Association]] moved kick-off to 16:00 instead on the same day.<ref>{{cite news|title=Community Shield: Kick-off time brought forward by 90 minutes after fan complaints|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65962426|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=20 June 2023|access-date=20 June 2023}}</ref> The match was televised live on [[ITV1]] and [[ITVX]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 June 2023 |title=ITV1 and ITVX to air 2023 Community Shield live |work=ITV |url=https://www.itv.com/football/articles/itv1-and-itvx-to-air-2023-community-shield-live |access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref>

[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] were the holders, having won the [[2022 FA Community Shield|2022 edition]], but they did not qualify for this match as they  finished fifth in the Premier League and were knocked out of the FA Cup in the fourth round.

==Background== 
{{main|2022–23 Arsenal F.C. season|2022–23 Manchester City F.C. season}}
[[File:Wembley Stadium interior.jpg|left|thumb|Wembley Stadium in London hosted the match]]
Manchester City qualified for the 2023 [[FA Community Shield]] as winners of the 2022–23 Premier League.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thomas-Humphreys |first=Harry |date=3 June 2023 |title=Who do Manchester City play in the Community Shield 2023? |work=Metro |publisher=DMG Media |url=https://metro.co.uk/2023/06/03/who-do-man-city-play-in-the-community-shield-2023-18892251/ |access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref> The club later faced [[Manchester derby|local rivals]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[2023 FA Cup final]], on course to complete a [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]].<ref>{{cite news |date=4 June 2023 |title=FA Cup final: Pep Guardiola talks treble at last after Man City beat Man Utd thanks to Ilkay Gundogan's double |publisher=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12895646/fa-cup-final-pep-guardiola-talks-treble-at-last-after-man-city-beat-man-utd-at-wembley-thanks-to-ilkay-gundogans-double |access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref> Manchester City defeated [[Erik ten Hag]]'s side to win their seventh FA Cup and as a result, Arsenal qualified for the 2023 FA Community Shield as Premier League runners-up. This was a rematch of the [[1934 FA Charity Shield]] and [[2014 FA Community Shield]], which Arsenal won {{nowrap|4–0}}<ref>{{cite news|title=Arsenal Win The F.A. Charity Shield|newspaper=The Times|date=29 November 1934|page=6}}</ref> and {{nowrap|3–0}},<ref>{{cite news|title=Arsenal 3–0 Manchester City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28647186|first=Mandeep|last=Sanghera|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=10 August 2014|access-date=30 October 2016}}</ref> respectively.

Arsenal were the home team of the match. The match returned to the home of English football in its 100th anniversary year after the [[2022 FA Community Shield|2022 edition]] was re-located to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]'s [[King Power Stadium]] due to the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2022 final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wembleystadium.com/events/2023/The-2023-Community-Shield |title=The 2023 FA Community Shield |publisher=Wembley Stadium |access-date=4 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/manchester-city-vs-arsenal/482389 |publisher=Sky Sports |title=News and Video Highlights – Arsenal vs. Man City |access-date=4 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/fa-community-shield/scores-fixtures/2023-08 |title=The FA Community Shield Scores & Fixtures |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=4 August 2023}}</ref>

==Match==
===Summary===
In the 77th minute, [[Cole Palmer]] put Manchester City into the lead after he received the ball on the right-hand side and then cut inside before curling a left-footed shot from just inside the penalty area into the left-hand corner of the net past [[Aaron Ramsdale]]. [[Leandro Trossard]] equalised for Arsenal in the 11th minute of stoppage time, after he tried an effort from just inside the penalty area which took a heavy deflection off defender [[Manuel Akanji]] which wrong-footed goalkeeper [[Stefan Ortega]] and ended up in the back of the net to make it 1–1 late on and send the match to a penalty shoot-out. [[Kevin De Bruyne]] and [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] both missed their penalties, which led to [[Fábio Vieira (footballer, born 2000)|Fábio Vieira]] scoring the winning penalty in the top left corner for Arsenal to win their fifth Community Shield in ten years.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2023/aug/06/arsenal-v-manchester-city-community-shield-live|title=Arsenal 1 Man City 1 (4-1 on pens): As it happened|date=6 August 2023|work=Guardian|accessdate=8 August 2023}}</ref>
